summary: No supplied-source defect breaks a stated invariant. Checked and holding: pillar instance order, hit-testing, foot-ring alignment and bounding spheres; symmetric lane routing for two-way mappings; per-arc dash distances that match the line segments; distinct, static threat-status dashes; the home view merging arcs by framework pair and mapping set, and focus showing exact group links; disposal of arc and sector geometry and materials; height animations that stop once settled; camera time steps capped after a long idle; agent and reduced-motion redraws that stop correctly. Two low-severity risks remain: color-only changes (Observatory lens) depend on something else waking the scene, and the layout observer wakes the scene for HUD changes that cannot move the panels.

findings.location: apps/web/src/scene/FrameworkScene.tsx:101-111 (same pattern in Beacons, Satellites, Crystals, Nexus PillarField)
findings.mechanism: With on-demand rendering, instance color writes in a layout effect show up only if a frame is requested. The height effect calls invalidate() (line 94), but the color effect does not. A lens-only change does not rebuild the scene labels (their memo has no lens dependency, lines 485-536), so the new colors appear only if something else happens to request a frame, such as the renderer noticing new inline handler functions or a HUD DOM change.
findings.evidence: Line 94 calls invalidate() after height targets change. Lines 101-111 call setColorAt and set needsUpdate, but never invalidate(). The SceneLabels memo dependencies are [layout, state, selectedId, hoveredId, focusIds, onSelect].
findings.recommendation: Call invalidate() at the end of the color and placement layout effects, and add a demand-rendering test that a lens-only change triggers a draw.

findings.mechanism: Any transform, margin or padding transition on any element inside a HUD panel adds the element to the transition set. The scene then redraws on every animation frame, and every label is re-measured, until the transition ends. A transform on a child cannot change the panel's on-screen rectangle, and the ResizeObserver on the panels already catches real size changes. Separately, any text change inside the stage root also triggers a re-measure and a redraw. A ticking readout or a button's hover animation therefore causes draw work while the scene itself is idle.
findings.evidence: Line 51 accepts any target with closest('[data-hud]'). Line 52's property list includes transform and padding. flush (lines 20-26) keeps rescheduling while the transition set is non-empty. Line 46 observes text changes and class/style changes across the whole root subtree.
findings.recommendation: Only track transitions whose target is a HUD panel itself or contains one. Ignore text changes inside [data-hud] unless panels are added or removed. Add a test that a transition on a HUD child does not start a redraw loop.

limitations: Not supplied, so not checked: spatialGeometry.ts (arcTriangles winding, hexRimGeometry), SpatialGround.tsx, colors.ts, global.css, the page and HUD components (CrosswalkPage, ObservatoryPage) and the useAgentActivity store.

Arc line width depends on the three.js version updating the line resolution before each draw. Arcs sets it in a useEffect without requesting a redraw, so on an older version a newly focused arc could be drawn once at the wrong width.

PillarField and UnitField rely on React Three Fiber rebuilding the instanced mesh when the instance count changes, while the other instanced components force a remount with a key. Correct handling depends on the library version.
Whether real HUD animations or readouts trigger finding 2 depends on CSS and page code that was not supplied.
Nothing was run and nothing was checked in a browser. The full integrated tests were still running when this review was done.
